title: Escalate retrieval for a named failure
description: Choose a query shape and a retrieval pattern. The lab checks the capabilities the pattern adds and counts its explicit online operations; it does not predict accuracy or latency.

scenarios.label: Exact identifier
scenarios.query: What does incident code PAY-4027 require?
scenarios.brief: The source uses the same rare identifier as the query.
scenarios.baselineFailure: Dense-only retrieval can rank semantically similar payment incidents above the exact code.

scenarios.label: Vocabulary gap
scenarios.query: How do we restart service after the main region disappears?
scenarios.brief: The runbook says regional failover and recovery sequence instead of restart or disappears.
scenarios.evidenceShape: One procedure expressed in different language
scenarios.baselineFailure: A literal query misses the runbook because the user and source use different terms.

scenarios.label: Cross-section policy
scenarios.query: Can a contractor export EU customer data during an incident?
scenarios.brief: The answer needs role permissions, residency policy, and an incident exception from different sections.
scenarios.evidenceShape: Three facts across two policy families
scenarios.baselineFailure: One nearest chunk answers only one part and hides the policy hierarchy.

scenarios.label: Mixed workload
scenarios.query: Route a stream of identifiers, policy questions, and multi-part research requests.
scenarios.brief: No single advanced pattern is justified for every request in this workload.
scenarios.evidenceShape: A route chosen per query, with a release gate
scenarios.baselineFailure: Always running the most expensive branch adds work and still cannot guarantee sufficient evidence.

capabilities.label: Exact language
capabilities.detail: Preserve rare identifiers and literal policy terms.

capabilities.label: Semantic match
capabilities.detail: Recover paraphrases whose wording differs from the source.

capabilities.label: Vocabulary bridge
capabilities.detail: Create an alternate representation for a persistent query-document language gap.

capabilities.label: Query decomposition
capabilities.detail: Split a multi-part question into bounded retrieval intents.

capabilities.label: Parent context
capabilities.detail: Recover the section or document hierarchy around a matching leaf.

capabilities.label: Source diversity
capabilities.detail: Keep independently useful evidence from being displaced by near duplicates.

capabilities.label: Query classification
capabilities.detail: Select a measured branch rather than using one pipeline for every request.

capabilities.label: Bounded retry
capabilities.detail: Permit a named fallback without creating an open-ended retrieval loop.

capabilities.label: Typed abstention
capabilities.detail: Return the missing evidence reason when no branch satisfies the release gate.

strategies.label: Single-pass hybrid
strategies.detail: Run lexical and dense retrieval once, fuse the two lists, and rerank a bounded pool.
strategies.failureSurface: One query can still miss a multi-part intent or document hierarchy.

strategies.label: Multi-query fusion
strategies.detail: Generate three bounded reformulations, run hybrid retrieval for each, then fuse rankings.
strategies.operationalCost: Eight search lists under these visible assumptions
strategies.failureSurface: Off-topic reformulations can pull irrelevant evidence into the candidate pool.

strategies.label: Hierarchical retrieval
strategies.detail: Route through document or section summaries, then retrieve leaf evidence under selected parents.
strategies.failureSurface: A poor parent selection can hide every relevant leaf below it.

strategies.label: HyDE
strategies.detail: Generate one hypothetical answer-shaped passage, embed it, then retrieve only real corpus documents.
strategies.operationalCost: One generation plus one dense search
strategies.failureSurface: A misleading hypothetical passage can steer retrieval toward the wrong neighborhood.

strategies.label: Adaptive router
strategies.detail: Classify the query, choose one bounded branch, evaluate evidence, and allow at most one fallback.
strategies.operationalCost: The displayed count is a four-search planning envelope, not a promise
strategies.failureSurface: Router and evidence-judge errors become new release dependencies.
